events.preview_text: Line up posts ahead without losing the slot for a timely local update.
events.body:
You can line up a week of posts in advance and still keep room for a timely update when something comes up in the shop.

Buffer is social media scheduling software that holds your posts in a queue — the order they'll go out. You build a few days ahead, so you're not hunting for something to say each morning.

The catch with planning ahead is usually the order. Post as you go and you scramble for something daily; commit to a fixed plan and there's no room for today's news without redoing the whole thing.

In Buffer you rearrange the queue by clicking and dragging. When something timely comes up, add it and the rest of the queue simply shifts down — so getting ahead doesn't mean locking yourself in.

Before you build a weekly queue, it's worth seeing what the Free plan covers. It lets you keep **10 scheduled posts per channel at a time**, which is enough to judge whether it fits a week of posting.

events.body:
You already run your shop's social yourself — deciding what goes out and when.

When you want to get a few posts ahead for a slow week, there's no easy way to see what's already lined up. So a timely local update means scrolling back to check you won't post twice, or just winging it.

Buffer is social scheduling software, and its calendar lays your scheduled posts across the week in one view. To slot in today's update, you drag posts into a new order — a quick change instead of re-planning the week.

That's what makes planning ahead feel less like admin: seeing the whole week is what makes a last-minute change easy.

Before you try a weekly queue, it's worth knowing the Free plan holds **10 scheduled posts per channel** at a time — a slot opens back up each time a post publishes. Worth a look to see whether that fits how many you'd line up.

events.body:
When you post your shop's social yourself, the hard part usually isn't posting — it's thinking of something worth saying on a morning you're already slammed.

Buffer is social media scheduling software that holds your posts in a queue: you write a few days' worth at once, in the order they'll go out, so no single morning depends on a fresh idea.

Then today happens — a last-minute sale, a change in hours. You click and drag that post to the front, and the rest of the queue shifts down. Foster Coffee Company works this way: planning posts ahead while still dropping in what's timely.

So getting ahead doesn't mean locking yourself in.

Looking at the Free plan builds nothing and commits to nothing — it's just the scheduling limit in plain sight. It keeps **10 scheduled posts per channel** at a time, enough to judge whether a week of posts fits before you set anything up.

events.subject: Plan ahead without locking yourself in
events.preview_text: Line up the week, then drag today's news to the front when it lands.
events.body:
You can plan your shop's posts ahead, or keep them loose for whatever today brings. Doing both has usually meant redoing the order by hand.

Buffer is social media scheduling software that holds your posts in a queue — you line up several in the order they'll go out, so the week is set without being stuck.

When something timely comes up — a last-minute sale, a change in hours — you **click and drag** that post to the front, and the rest of the queue shifts down. You stay ahead and still react to today.

Foster Coffee Company runs this way: the queue lets them deliver posts consistently while keeping room to change things at the last minute.

Before you set anything up, the Free plan shows its scheduling limit plainly — **10 scheduled posts per channel** at a time. That's enough to judge whether a week's queue fits.
